title: Blue Ocean Minang Run 2026: Padang's Sold-Out Coastal Birthday Bash
seo_title: Blue Ocean Minang Run 2026 Review: Padang Half Marathon
meta_description: A honest look at Blue Ocean Minang Run 2026 in Padang: sold-out 21K/10K/5K/2K/1K race along Pantai Padang, course, prep and who it suits.
dek: Padang's homegrown beach-and-hills race has grown from a 2,000-runner alumni project into a sold-out city birthday centerpiece — here's what to expect on race morning.
verdict: Blue Ocean Minang Run works best as a destination weekend rather than a PB hunt: a scenic coastal 21K with real hill work, wrapped in a city-wide birthday festival with genuine local government backing. It suits travelling runners chasing an Indonesian city-and-sea experience, families using the kids/lansia categories, and mid-pack half marathoners who don't mind a tougher back half. Sharp-elbowed competitors chasing fast times on a flat course should look elsewhere — the appeal here is atmosphere and terrain variety, not a record-friendly layout.

sections.heading: The Course: Beach Start, Hill Finish
paragraphs: Race morning begins at 05:00 WIB along the Pantai Padang strip near Danau Cimpago, with five distances on offer: 1K, 2K, 5K, 10K and the flagship 21K [1]. Organisers are upfront that the half marathon is the category to respect rather than the one to take lightly on effort, since it is the route built to cross hills and one of the city's iconic bridges rather than stay flat along the sand [1]. That framing matters for pacing plans — this is not a beachfront time-trial course, it's a half marathon with genuine terrain variety folded into a coastal setting.

The 2025 edition offers a useful preview of what a Padang-city loop looks like in practice: runners started at Pantai Purus, threaded through the old town (Kota Tua), climbed toward Gunung Padang, and returned to finish back at Pantai Purus [5]. Reporting on the 2026 build-up describes a similarly city-spanning route touching Kota Tua and Bukit Gado-Gado, reinforcing that the organisers keep leaning into Padang's mix of coastline, colonial-era streets and hill terrain rather than a simple out-and-back [3]. Expect a course that trades pancake-flat splits for sightseeing and a workout.

Cut-off windows are generous for the shorter, family-oriented categories: 1.5 hours for the 5K 'Enjoy' category, 2.5 hours for the 10K 'Eksotis' field, one hour for the 2K kids' race, and 30 minutes for the 1K Lansia (senior) single or double entries [1]. That spread signals an event genuinely built to include walkers, kids and older participants alongside the competitive 21K field, not just a half marathon with token short races bolted on.

sections.heading: Build-Up and Organisation
paragraphs: Ahead of the 2025 running, Padang's public works department (PUPR) sent crews out the night before race day specifically to drain standing water and patch flood-prone stretches along the route, including sections near Rusunawa and Hotel Mercure, so that runners and spectators heading to Pantai Padang wouldn't have to deal with pooled water underfoot [5]. That kind of targeted municipal prep is a good sign for a tropical coastal course where drainage is a real recurring issue between editions.

For 2026, the event has been formally elevated: city hall named BOM Run the main event of Padang's 357th anniversary celebrations, with the race weekend running alongside the city's broader 'Taste of Padang Experience' birthday programme from 7 to 9 August [4]. That civic backing extends beyond a photo-op ribbon-cutting — the city government has instructed its full roster of departments and civil servants to actively support the event's success [4], which in past-edition terms translated into the kind of road and drainage work described above.

sections.heading: Atmosphere, Growth and Competitiveness
paragraphs: The event's trajectory is genuinely steep. The 2025 edition drew more than 2,200 registered runners around an original alumni-association target of 2,000 [5], while the 2026 edition set its sights on roughly 6,000 participants drawn from across Indonesia and, organisers hope, the wider ASEAN region [1]. Registration for 2026 has since closed out entirely, with the race now listed as sold out — a clear jump in demand from the prior year's numbers.

On-the-ground accounts from the 2025 race describe a crowded, upbeat start along Pantai Purus with runners arriving from well beyond West Sumatra, mixing serious time-chasers with people simply there for the coastal scenery and city atmosphere [6]. One finisher captured that dual appeal bluntly: "Ini kegiatan yang luar biasa," describing the event as proof that sport can drive real local economic impact [6]. That's broadly the tone BOM Run is chasing — festival energy layered onto a genuine road race, rather than a purely competitive time-trial atmosphere.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you're weighing this race for 2027 or a future edition, the profile is clear: strong municipal support, a course that actually uses Padang's coastline, old town and hills rather than looping a car park, and cut-offs generous enough to welcome kids and senior runners alongside the half marathon field [1,5]. The trade-off is that the 21K is explicitly built to test stamina on climbs rather than deliver a fast, flat PB course [1], so runners chasing a personal best on paper-flat asphalt may want a different target race.

For anyone drawn to sport tourism — pairing a half marathon or 10K with a coastal Sumatran city, its old-town streets and a genuine civic celebration around it — BOM Run 2026's 9 August date and sold-out status suggest the organisers are onto something that's resonating well beyond the original alumni-association crowd that launched it [1,4]. Book early for future editions; this one filled up.

faqs.question: When is Blue Ocean Minang Run 2026 and where does it start?
faqs.answer: It runs Sunday, 9 August 2026, starting at 05:00 WIB along Pantai Padang near Danau Cimpago, part of Padang's 357th anniversary celebrations held 7–9 August [1,4]. It offers 21.1K, 10K, 5K, 2K, and 1K.

faqs.question: Can I still register for BOM Run 2026?
faqs.answer: No — registration for the 2026 edition is officially listed as sold out, following ticket tiers on Eztix that progressively closed out ahead of race day. It's held at Kota Padang, Sumatera Barat. It offers 21.1K, 10K, 5K, 2K, and 1K.

faqs.question: What distances does Blue Ocean Minang Run offer?
faqs.answer: Five categories: 1K, 2K, 5K, 10K and the flagship 21K half marathon, catering to kids, seniors ('Lansia'), casual 5K runners and competitive half marathoners alike [1]. Registration has closed. It's held at Kota Padang, Sumatera Barat.

faqs.question: Is the 21K course hilly or difficult?
faqs.answer: Yes. Organisers describe the half marathon as the toughest category, built to cross hills and one of Padang's iconic bridges and genuinely test runner stamina rather than stay flat along the beach [1].
